item.title: security: ​​Beyond source code: A path to the keys to the kingdom
item.description:
Microsoft describes how Storm-3068 used a compromised identity to expand access into cloud environments, moving beyond source code exposure to broader infrastructure compromise. The post focuses on defensive steps for protecting identities, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: From guidance to action: Security fundamentals that materially reduce risk
item.description:
Microsoft says AI has changed the cybersecurity operating environment and points readers to exposure management guidance with recommended controls. The post emphasizes taking action on security fundamentals to reduce risk.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: How to secure edge AI in customer-owned environments
item.description:
Microsoft says edge AI deployments in customer-owned environments require stronger verification of systems, software, and AI assets before sharing sensitive data, credentials, or models. The post frames secure edge AI as a trust and validation problem for third-party environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Impersonating IT support: how threat actors turn a remote session into enterprise-wide access
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported a human-operated intrusion campaign that abuses Microsoft Teams external collaboration to impersonate IT support, gain remote access, and deploy a Node.js-based implant. The campaign uses social engineering and legitimate tools to move from initial access to lateral movement, with Microsoft Defender used for detection and disruption.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Hunting MacSync Stealer infrastructure through behavioral pivots
item.description:
Microsoft describes how it tracked MacSync Stealer infrastructure despite rapid domain rotation by using stable behavioral pivots. The investigation identified more than 30 related domains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: From open lures to cloaked gates: How a macOS ClickFix campaign learned to hide
item.description:
Microsoft describes a macOS ClickFix campaign that changed from openly delivering infostealer lures to placing them behind a browser-fingerprinting gate. The shift reduces visibility of the malicious infrastructure but also creates new detection opportunities for defenders.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Email threat landscape: Q2 2026 trends and insights
item.description:
Microsoft reports that Q2 2026 saw continued declines in several phishing techniques after disruption of the Tycoon2FA platform. Attackers shifted toward Teams-based social engineering and more automated, multi-stage attack chains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
